title: Extraction of Non-Structural Carbohydrates in Plant Tissues
author: Lynn Doran
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.b2jmqck6
materials: After combining the last ethanolic supernatant, remove the ethanol using a Speed Vac Concencentrator, following manufacturers recommendations. Thermo-Fisher SPD12 Speed-Vac at 0.1 HPr, 35 °C , and Thermo-Fisher RVT404 refrigerated vapor trap -108 °C . Ensure Speed-Vac is properly balanced. Ideally samples would be run at 30 °C but the lowest temperature setting on this instrument was 35 °C . Warmer temperatures could degrade sugars and damage sample integrity.

steps.title: Label and weigh sample
steps.instruction: Weigh 10–15 mg of freeze‑dried, pulverized plant material into a labeled 2 mL screw‑cap tube and record the weight; label both tube side and lid with a unique ID.

steps.title: Add ethanol solvent
steps.instruction: Add 1 mL of 80 % ethanol to each tube (a repeat pipettor is useful for many samples).

steps.title: Mix sample with ethanol
steps.instruction: Vortex the tube until all powder is dissolved.

steps.title: Heat incubation
steps.instruction: Incubate the tubes in an 80 °C water bath for 20 min; if using snap‑cap tubes, place a weight on top to prevent caps from opening due to ethanol evaporation (a microtube rack is sufficient; screw‑cap lids need no weight).

steps.title: Centrifuge to pellet solids
steps.instruction: Centrifuge at maximum speed (>15 000 g) for 3 min to precipitate solids.

steps.title: Collect supernatant
steps.instruction: Decant the supernatant into a labeled 8 mL tube. If the pellet sticks, pour directly; if not, centrifuge again and pipette off the liquid phase.

steps.title: Repeat ethanol washes
steps.instruction: Repeat steps 2–6 four to six times (four washes are usually sufficient for leaves), combining all supernatants from the same sample into the same labeled 8 mL tube after each centrifugation.

steps.title: Store ethanolic extracts
steps.instruction: Keep the 8 mL supernatant tubes on ice or at 4 °C while the tissue incubates at 80 °C; after all washes, store the combined ethanolic supernatant at –20 °C for several months.

steps.title: Dry the pellet
steps.instruction: After the final ethanol removal, leave lids off and dry the remaining pellet.

substeps.instruction: Dry at 40 °C overnight; if a 40 °C oven is unavailable, dry at 30 °C then at 58 °C for 2–3 h the next day.

Alternatively, place the tube in a Speed‑Vac concentrator (Thermo‑Fisher SPD12 recommended) and run until dry (≈16 h to remove 4 mL ethanol). Load samples the night before and finish the next afternoon.

steps.title: Store dried pellet
steps.instruction: After the pellet is dry, replace the lids; the dried starch pellet can be stored at room temperature (or at –20 °C for long‑term storage).

steps.title: Re‑hydrate sugars
steps.instruction: Add 1 mL of distilled or MilliQ water to the dried sugars in the tube.

steps.title: Transfer from polystyrene tubes
steps.instruction: If the tube is polystyrene, transfer the aqueous solution to a chemical‑resistant tube (polypropylene, polyethylene, or glass). If a resistant tube was used initially, continue in the same tube (organic solvents melt polystyrene).

steps.title: Dissolve sugars completely
steps.instruction: Vortex for 30 s, then use a Pasteur pipette to pipette vigorously, ensuring all sugars dissolve.

steps.title: Ice‑bath shaking
steps.instruction: Place the tubes in an ice bath on a plate shaker for 1 h to aid dissolution.

steps.title: Transfer aqueous solution
steps.instruction: Transfer the entire aqueous sugar solution to a new labeled chemical‑resistant tube (e.g., a 2 mL polypropylene or polyethylene microcentrifuge tube).

steps.title: Add chloroform for pigment extraction
steps.instruction: Add 500 µL chloroform; prime the pipette tip by filling with 500 µL chloroform, ejecting it back into the reagent container, and refilling before dispensing.

steps.title: Mix with chloroform
steps.instruction: Vortex the tube.

steps.title: Phase separation
steps.instruction: Centrifuge at maximum speed (>15 000 g) for 1 min to separate solvent phases.

steps.title: Collect aqueous phase
steps.instruction: Transfer only the upper aqueous phase to a new labeled 2 mL tube.

steps.title: Final storage
steps.instruction: Store the aqueous extract at –20 °C for up to several months.
